clue.text: Warplane circling about cargo ship

indicators.note: the warplane goes round the word for about, so it surrounds that piece

parts.note: a fighter is a combat aircraft
re is Latin-derived for concerning or about

explanation.surface: A military jet circles a merchant vessel at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a vessel built to carry goods, synonym for a cargo ship.

clue.text: Fine one's collected in the end

indicators.note: the fine and the one's pieces gather the little word in between them

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
one's read as one is gives I plus IS
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine has been gathered up at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Finis is the Latin word printed at the close of a book or film, meaning conclusion.

clue.text: Where films were made the Spanish way? Not quite

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article

indicators.note: the word for way stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: a street is a road or way

explanation.surface: A film location asks whether movies were made in Spanish fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: ELSTREE is a town north of London famous for its film studios; 'Not quite' cuts the final T from STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree in Hertfordshire housed major British film studios for decades, so it is a place of movie production.

clue.text: Goalie oddly holding blue blouse

indicators.note: the odd letters grip the synonym for blue between them
take the odd-numbered letters of the keeper's word: first, third, fifth

parts.note: blue jokes are risqué, i.e. ribald

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper strangely clutches a blue blouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' here means risqué, not sad or a colour; a Garibaldi blouse copies the red shirts of the Italian patriot's army.
explanation.definitionFit: A Garibaldi is a loose high-necked blouse modelled on the red shirts of the Italian patriot's followers.

clue.text: I'm set to move to old-fashioned place in New York

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are set moving into a new order

parts.note: a square is a conventional, unfashionable person

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are ready to relocate somewhere quaint in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges I'M SET into TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Times Square is the famous plaza in Manhattan, so it is a location in New York.

clue.text: Gem cut for fabulous bird

indicators.note: the gem word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: rock is slang for a gem, especially a diamond

explanation.surface: A precious stone is cut for a mythical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the K of ROCK; the 'fabulous' is of fable, not of excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend, a creature of fable.

clue.text: Key failure getting teeth cleaner

parts.note: F is a musical key
a loss is a failure or defeat

explanation.surface: Missing a crucial point leads to dental hygiene.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental floss is thread used to clean between the teeth.

clue.text: King imprisoned by duke at the outset

indicators.note: the king letter is locked inside the duke word

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, so a duke is a fist
R is from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is jailed by a duke right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duke' is not a nobleman: in slang 'put up your dukes' means raise your fists.
explanation.definitionFit: First as an adverb means initially, before anything else, the same as at the outset.

clue.text: A rounded character, but not initially amusing man

indicators.note: the amusing word loses its opening letter

parts.note: comic means funny or amusing
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A plump personality turns out not, at first, to be a funny fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a Greek letter; omicron is a round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the Greek letter O, whose written form is a circle, hence a rounded character.

clue.text: She cleans, working for steward

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman is employed in place of a household manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A seneschal was the steward who ran a medieval noble household.

clue.text: Recall one hundred odd swallowing singular medicine?

indicators.note: the pieces take the singular letter inside them
to recall is to call back, so the hundred word runs backwards

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: Remember one hundred strange things being swallowed as remedies?
explanation.walkthrough: A nostrum is a patent remedy of doubtful worth, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, hence the question mark on a dubious medicine.

clue.text: What's vulture looking for to keep going? Last bit of prey, for one

indicators.note: one stands in for that final letter

parts.note: carry on means to continue or keep going

indicators.note: take only the closing letter of the hunted word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vulture searches on and on for what remains of its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' swaps I for Y, the last bit of prey, in CARRY ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrion is dead flesh, which scavenging vultures seek out to eat.

clue.text: Clean axe

definitions.meaning: to wash something by rubbing hard
to cancel or call off a plan

explanation.definitionFit: Scrub means both to clean by vigorous rubbing and, informally, to cancel or axe.

clue.text: Principal performers get going with containers of tea

parts.note: to start is to begin or get going
urns are large vessels for serving tea

explanation.surface: The headline acts begin with tea urns.
explanation.definitionFit: Star turns are the main acts on a variety bill, the leading performers.

clue.text: A heartless lie succeeded stopping trouble from fans

indicators.note: the lie word loses its central letter

parts.note: a fiction is an invented falsehood
ado is fuss or trouble
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded, here stopping or closing off the trouble word

explanation.surface: Fans are told a heartless lie which then ended the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle T of FICTION, giving FICION.
explanation.definitionFit: Aficionados are keen enthusiasts or devotees of an activity, synonym for fans.

clue.text: Times reportedly producing an extra

indicators.note: the word for times is heard spoken, pointing to a word sounding the same

parts.note: by is used for multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A newspaper is said to be publishing a supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means multiplied by; a BYE in cricket is a run scored without the bat touching the ball, counted among the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye is a run not off the bat, which is recorded as one of the extras.

clue.text: Fetch feathers from floor

parts.note: to fetch is to bring
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Fetch the feathers off the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is the verb, to knock someone to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor an opponent is to knock them over, to bring them down.

clue.text: What the pub not serving grub has to offer around one?

definitions.text: What the pub not serving grub has to offer around one?

parts.words: What the pub not serving grub has to offer around one?
parts.note: a midday meal taken as drinks only, which is all a pub with no food could provide at lunchtime

explanation.surface: A pub without food asks what it can offer at one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around one' means at about 1 pm, lunchtime, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid lunch is a midday break spent drinking alcohol instead of eating.

clue.text: Comes down on head causing a scene

parts.note: an aircraft lands when it comes down
a cape or headland juts into the sea

explanation.surface: Something landing on its head causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a scene' looks like a fuss but is a view; 'head' is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a view of countryside, a scene in a painting or in nature.

clue.text: Fancy one state employing sorcerers

indicators.note: the one and state pieces take the sorcerers into their service, holding them inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a nation is a state
magi are wise men or magicians

explanation.surface: A fanciful country hires wizards.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as a noun is the faculty of imagining, the creative power of the mind.

clue.text: Country's saint — head of Ignatius on top of arch

parts.note: St Alban is the first British Christian martyr

indicators.note: take the opening letter of the saint's name Ignatius
take the opening letter of the curved structure word

explanation.surface: A nation's patron saint stands beneath an arch with Ignatius at its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is': the country is ALBAN plus I plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a country in the Balkans on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Come together on being taken over

indicators.note: taken over means turned over, so the cricket word runs backwards

parts.note: on is the cricket name for the leg side

explanation.surface: Two groups merge after one takes over the other.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is for things or people to unite and work well, to come together.

clue.text: Cosmonaut runs into acceleration due to gravity once more

parts.note: g is the physics symbol for this acceleration

indicators.note: the runs letter goes inside the once more word

parts.note: again means once more
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A spaceman again breaks into high-g forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin was the Soviet cosmonaut who became the first human in space in 1961.

clue.text: Start to gamble with small northern broker

parts.note: to go is to start, as in ready, steady, go
a bet is a gamble
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A small northern broker starts off gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary who brokers dealings between two parties.

clue.text: Girl put up paintings around small house

indicators.note: the turned art word goes around the house abbreviation
in a down light, put up means written upwards, so the paintings word runs backwards

parts.note: art means works such as paintings
ho is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A girl hangs paintings round her little house.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'put up' signals reading upwards, so the paintings word goes in backwards before the house goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thora is a girl's given name, as in the actress Thora Hird.

clue.text: A male, one in G and S, all-round as character?

indicators.note: the whole sequence turns right round, reading backwards
the one letter sits inside the G and S pair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Is a man who appears in Gilbert and Sullivan an all-round personality?
explanation.walkthrough: G and S looks like Gilbert and Sullivan, but they are the bare letters; the character is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a written character.

clue.text: Acknowledge miners' leader must enter mine passage

indicators.note: the leader letter goes inside the passage word

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine

indicators.note: take the opening letter of the miners' word

explanation.surface: The miners' union leader has to go down the mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to concede or own up to it, to acknowledge.

clue.text: Shot a line after private's action that backfired?

indicators.note: the shot pieces come after the private piece

parts.note: one's own things are private to oneself
a go is an attempt, a shot

explanation.surface: A soldier fires a line after a private action goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' is not a soldier but 'own'; an OWN GOAL is a goal scored against one's own side.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal, literally scoring for the opponents, figuratively means an act that harms its doer.

clue.text: A secretion of blackflies

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out of the letters of the insect word

explanation.surface: Blackflies produce a secretion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lac is the resinous substance secreted by lac insects, used to make shellac.

clue.text: Sarcastic remark about a zodiac sign in chart

indicators.note: the remark word wraps round the a

parts.note: a dig is a pointed, cutting comment
the Ram is Aries in the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone makes a sarcastic comment about a star sign on a horoscope chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawing that sets out information, such as a chart.

clue.text: Name a song about an antelope

indicators.note: turn the a-and-song pieces about, so they read backwards

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: Name a song all about an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses A LAY into YALA.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Fruit ready by cask we brought round

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash

indicators.note: the cask and we pieces turn round, reading backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit is ready beside a cask that we roll round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for money, as in 'the ready'; a tun is an old large wine cask.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew nut is the edible kernel of the cashew fruit, classed as a fruit botanically.
